bottom_line: In Val-HeFT, valsartan vs placebo added to background heart-failure therapy reduced the combined end point of mortality and morbidity (relative risk, 0.87; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.77 to 0.97).
implications: These results support that, in this trial population, valsartan (vs placebo) reduced the risk of the combined mortality–morbidity end point (relative risk, 0.87; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.77 to 0.97) while not changing all-cause mortality (relative risk, 1.02; 0.88–1.18). They also support that discontinuations due to adverse events were higher with valsartan (9.9 percent vs 7.2 percent).

major_points.quote: The Valsartan Heart Failure Trial (Val-HeFT) was a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel-group trial.

major_points.text: 5010 patients with NYHA class II–IV heart failure were randomized to valsartan 160 mg twice daily or placebo twice daily.
major_points.quote: A total of 5010 patients with heart failure of New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II, III, or IV were randomly assigned to receive 160 mg of valsartan or placebo twice daily.

major_points.text: Primary outcomes were mortality and a combined end point of mortality and morbidity (cardiac arrest with resuscitation, HF hospitalization, or ≥4 hours of IV inotropes/vasodilators).
major_points.quote: The primary outcomes were mortality and the combined end point of mortality and morbidity, defined as the incidence of cardiac arrest with resuscitation, hospitalization for heart failure, or receipt of intravenous inotropic or vasodilator therapy for at least four hours.

major_points.text: Overall mortality was similar between groups.
major_points.quote: Mortality was similar in the two treatment groups (Fig. 1 and Table 2).

major_points.text: Valsartan reduced the combined end point compared with placebo (RR 0.87; 97.5% CI 0.77 to 0.97; P=0.009).
major_points.quote: a 13.2 percent reduction in risk with valsartan (relative risk, 0.87; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.77 to 0.97) (Table 2).

major_points.text: Adverse events leading to discontinuation were more common with valsartan than placebo (9.9% vs 7.2%; P<0.001).
major_points.quote: Adverse events leading to the discontinuation of the drug occurred in 249 of the patients receiving valsartan (9.9 percent) and 181 patients receiving placebo (7.2 percent) (P<0.001).

absolute_effects.text: Combined end point: 723 (28.8 percent) with valsartan vs 801 (32.1 percent) with placebo.
Death from any cause (during entire trial): 495 (19.7 percent) with valsartan vs 484 (19.4 percent) with placebo.

subgroups.text: Interaction by baseline ACE-inhibitor/beta-blocker use was statistically significant for mortality (P=0.009) and the combined end point (P=0.001).

inclusion_criteria.text: Men and women 18 years old or older with a history and clinical findings of heart failure for at least three months before screening.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Men and women 18 years old or older with a history and clinical findings of heart failure for at least three months before screening were eligible.

inclusion_criteria.text: Heart failure of NYHA class II, III, or IV and clinically stable.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients had heart failure of New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II, III, or IV and were clinically stable.

inclusion_criteria.text: Receiving for at least two weeks a fixed-dose drug regimen that could include ACE inhibitors, diuretics, digoxin, and beta-blockers.
inclusion_criteria.quote: To be eligible, they had to have been receiving for at least two weeks a fixed-dose drug regimen that could include ACE inhibitors, diuretics, digoxin, and beta-blockers.

inclusion_criteria.text: Documented LV dysfunction with EF <40% and LV dilatation with short-axis internal dimension at end diastole >2.9 cm/m2.
inclusion_criteria.quote: documented left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of less than 40 percent and left ventricular dilatation with an echocardiographically measured short-axis internal dimension at end diastole greater than 2.9 cm per square meter
